claims.statement: Self-hosted runners recommended only for private repositories because public forks can submit PR workflow code that compromises host. Recommendation is not absolute platform prohibition or proof private workloads trusted.

All major/minor/patch runner releases count as updates; after30days without update no jobs queued, and critical security update blocks queuing until updated. No update disabled/applied, exact release freshness separately needed.

Custom label creation through runner settings creates and assigns label; labels may be unassigned but not manually deleted, with unused-label lifecycle in separate reusable. Not actual host capability verification or authorized mutation.

Self-hosted setup requires machine access; GHES additionally Actions enabled by site administrator and ports/protocols include. Registration prerequisites are not instance enablement approval or observed readiness.
Service tutorial asks to add client.js with following code, whose body is outside this fragment. File instruction not executed; standalone fragment cannot certify client source.
Service example uses ubuntu-latest Docker host, labelled GitHub-hosted only outside GHES. On GHES workflow label does not prove hosted-runner support.
Service example runs job in node:20-bookworm-slim with ubuntu-latest Docker host, hosted only outside GHES. Mutable image tag/external link not image provenance or actual service execution.
Localhost/127.0.0.1 hostname applies in enclosing host-networking example, not universal service connectivity from sibling/job containers.
Service use requires understanding network differences between host jobs and container jobs; linked full guidance is separately reviewed.
Service workflow stages checkout, dependency installation and client creation script. Description is not verified connection, dependency trust or installation authorization.
Runner-group selection click identifies parent target but gives no management permission or observed configuration.
Runner-name selection UI may be ambiguous across scopes; actual stable identity and permissions remain separately validated.

setup-node creates .npmrc registry/scope configuration and accepts authentication input for private access/publication according to source. Token channel/action implementation remain separately reviewed; no file or credential generated.
Environment sidebar navigation is a UI route only, not configured or enforced deployment protection.
Security > Secrets and variables > Actions navigation does not prove role access or secret existence.

Hosted runner new-VM statement explicitly excludes single-CPU runners, which run containers on shared VMs. Fresh image descriptions elsewhere must not imply dedicated VM isolation for single-CPU jobs.
Single-CPU row describes Linux1CPU,5GB RAM,14GB SSD,x64 and ubuntu-slim linked image. Parent public/private table placement and container/shared-VM exception require preserved context.
Hosted private networking does not support static IP addresses for larger runners. This is private-networking constraint, distinct from standalone larger-runner static-IP capability.

Public standard runner guidance claims free/unlimited use with associated label specifications, subject to other workflow limits; shared-VM single-CPU include remains an isolation exception. Pricing/source claims are pinned, not verified current charges or cost authority.

Public x64 Linux4CPU/16GB RAM/14GB SSD labels ubuntu-latest,24.04,22.04,26.04; Windows same dimensions labels windows-latest,2025,2025-vs2026,2022. Image links on mutable main are not immutable provenance.
Public arm64 Linux and Windows rows each4CPU/16GB RAM/14GB SSD; Ubuntu22.04/24.04/26.04-arm and Windows11/11-vs2026-arm labels. Architecture-specific images not universally compatible actions.

Public macOS Intel4CPU/14GB RAM/14GB SSD uses15-intel/26-intel; M1arm64 three CPUs/7GB RAM/14GB SSD uses latest,14,15,26 and preview xcode27. latest points at26 in source links, distinct from larger-runner table's15-latest wording.

Private and conditionally GHEC internal standard runners consume account minutes then per-minute charges. Linux/Windows x64 each2CPU/8GB RAM/14GB SSD; Ubuntu labels same as public, Windows latest/2025/2022 excluding public2025-vs2026 entry.

Private/internal arm64 Linux and Windows each2CPU/8GB RAM/14GB SSD with same listed architecture labels. windows-11-vs2026-arm linked image path differs from the public row (Arm64-VS2026 versus VS2026-Arm64), requiring linked identity review.

Private/internal macOS rows retain Intel4CPU/14GB and M1threeCPU/7GB with14GB SSD and corresponding labels/preview; GHEC includes data-residency macOS unavailability. Single-CPU row also included despite prose saying all private runners VMs, a source composition inconsistency.

Unspecified Linux/macOS shell uses bash -e with sh fallback; explicit Bash adds no-profile/no-rc and pipefail, Windows uses Git Bash. Thus explicit versus default Bash differs in failure detection, not interchangeable.
All-platform pwsh executes dot-sourced ps1 script, Python executes script, and Linux/macOS sh uses sh -e. Command templates are inert evidence, not verified local shell execution.

Windows cmd uses cmd extension and ComSpec CALL template; default pwsh may fallback to PowerShell Desktop on self-hosted without Core; explicit powershell uses Desktop. Preserve platform scope/extension and do not assume identical error semantics.
